Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed mass in the right upper lung field with homogeneous opacity and smooth margins, lacking the spiculation or ill-defined borders typical of primary bronchogenic carcinoma. This morphological appearance is consistent with the description of a pleuropulmonary synovial sarcoma (PPSS), which often presents as a large, well-defined soft tissue mass.
